questions.text: If I raise a genuine safeguarding concern and it turns out I was wrong, am I going to get in trouble for it?
Is the whistleblowing hotline different at each site, or is it the same number everywhere?
How many cases does it actually take before an outbreak gets declared?
Once there are no new cases, how long before an outbreak is actually declared over?
If a resident's attorney seems to be spending their money oddly, who outside Alderbridge actually gets involved?
If an allegation against a staff member turns out to be unfounded, what happens to that staff member?
Has the time allowed for an on-site search before calling the police changed recently?
How quickly does the LADO actually get contacted after an allegation now?
How far ahead of a DoLS expiry does it get flagged to the local authority?
Is it still okay for someone to start their first shift if the right-to-work check hasn't quite been finished yet?
Has the Homely Remedies Policy actually changed, or just been retitled?
Do staff still just eyeball the sling before a hoist transfer, or is there more to the pre-use check now?
If a hoist is found to be damaged, can it just be set aside until someone gets round to fixing it?
How far can a resident's window actually open under the restrictor policy these days?
Can any member of staff release a window restrictor in an emergency?
How often is a backup actually test-restored now?
Would Alderbridge's backups survive a ransomware attack that got into the network?
Is there an actual external agency to report a scam against a resident to, or does that just stay internal?
Can staff at Riverside House still wear the branded fleece instead of the tunic?
Was there an earlier version of the Outbreak Management Procedure, and if so what did it used to say?
Has my right-to-work follow-up check actually gone through yet?
Can you just confirm my DoLS authorisation has been renewed?
Quick one: how long before an immediate on-site search escalates to calling the police for a missing resident, and separately, how far can a window actually open under the restrictor policy?
If my colleague's allegation about me turns out to be unfounded, are they in any trouble for raising it, and how fast would the LADO have been told about it?
Is 'Nightingale Protocol Seven' one of our actual radio codes here?
Do we log controlled drug discrepancies on a form called TF-CD-9?
For today's fire door audit, what should I actually be checking on each door?
What exactly happens once a DoLS authorisation's expiry is getting close and nobody's heard back?
What's the very first thing staff do once someone's realised a resident isn't where they should be?
If the decision is made not to suspend someone during an allegation investigation, does anyone double-check that decision now?
